RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 4

An all-woman panel chose a woman over another woman. Sex can't easily explain a decision where the winner and the runner-up share it, so the panel's composition is not evidence of anything here — and raising it would likely read as a weak, scattershot grievance that undermines your stronger points.

Your real points are substantive: the appointee has a master's against your PhD, and "broad experience of regulatory affairs" is vague next to nine years of modelling. Ask again, in writing, for the selection criteria, the scoring, and how each candidate was ranked against them. Set a deadline and note any internal appeal route or applicable time limit.

If something else fits — age, for instance — pursue that specifically.
